technical_hypothesis.primary_training_data_risk: labels such as warranty eligibility, root cause, responsible trade, severity, and recurrence are created after inspection and often reflect inconsistent local coding; using final diagnosis, repair, supplier liability, or claim outcome at intake time would cause leakage

training_data.observation_unit: one post-handover request or one building-condition inspection candidate at the decision point
training_data.input_data: only attributes available before inspection, such as project, building system, unit age, request channel, resident description category, previous related requests, warranty matrix, maintenance evidence availability, and current queue context
training_data.target_or_reward: confirmed technical category, procedence, recurrence within a defined future window, or inspection escalation confirmed by an engineer
training_data.label_source: closed service orders, signed inspection reports, and quality-engineering records; consistency is unknown until sampled
training_data.prediction_time: after structured intake and before technical inspection or prioritization
training_data.expected_volume: unknown; must be measured per developer and pooled only after taxonomy compatibility is proven
training_data.class_balance: unknown; safety-relevant and materially recurrent defects are expected to be minority classes but must not be assumed
training_data.historical_coverage: unknown; likely fragmented across CRM, post-handover platforms, spreadsheets, and contractor records
training_data.train_validation_split: time-based and project-based holdouts to test transfer across buildings, suppliers, materials, and delivery cohorts
training_data.leakage_risks: final inspection result, warranty approval, repair type, supplier chargeback, closure status, customer satisfaction, and fields corrected after escalation
training_data.representativeness_risks: different building standards, regional climate, materials, contractors, resident reporting behavior, maintenance compliance, and coding practices
training_data.feedback_loop: engineer-confirmed corrections may improve labels, but model-prioritized inspections can distort which cases receive detailed diagnosis
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: minimize resident identifiers and free text; preserve engineer authority for safety, warranty, liability, and repair decisions
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: structured intake, deterministic warranty and severity rules, duplicate detection, dashboards, and engineer-defined queues

portfolio_comparison.reason: The candidate is a generic intake classification or review-priority variant. Existing post-handover products already centralize structured claims, warranty rules, inspection scheduling, evidence, SLA, recurrence indicators, and assisted triage; the remaining learned score does not create a distinct bounded outcome or architecture.

existing_landscape.summary: Adopt or configure established post-handover and maintenance platforms, standardize defect and outcome taxonomies, and use deterministic warranty and safety rules before considering a local supervised model.
